title: Transient heat to global Arrhenius creep contract
purpose: Verify that prescribed and physical-time temperature fields are evaluated at the shared creep quadrature identity and consumed by the same backward-Euler update, temperature-resolved elastic response, thermal strain, analytical tangent, Newton path, rollback, output, and checkpoint identity as the global power-law creep state.
physics: three-dimensional small-strain Mises power-law creep with prescribed or time-varying Arrhenius temperature fields

execution.evidence: A unit-cube relaxation patch carries prescribed or synthetic temperature fields, and a separate three-dimensional component test solves transient heat first and passes its accepted physical-time history directly to global creep. The accepted integration-point temperature range and nonuniform equivalent creep strain are retained in the structured result.

observables: TEMP is present as the finite-element field supplied to the constitutive step.
Every accepted increment records the minimum and maximum temperature evaluated at creep quadrature points.
The hotter and colder integration points develop different CEEQ under the same imposed displacement path.
The temperature description participates in checkpoint compatibility.
A solved physical-time heat history is interpolated at each creep increment endpoint and becomes part of the step summary.
The nodal history archive is restored in both two-rank-to-one-rank and one-rank-to-two-rank directions.
acceptance: All consumed temperatures are finite and positive kelvin values.
Quadrature extrema lie strictly inside the 800--900 K nodal range and preserve its symmetric mean.
The global step converges and the CEEQ field is nonuniform.
Temperature extrema are available both as quantities and accepted-increment histories.
limitations: The internal component contract is not an external power-component validation case.

Temperature-dependent E, nu and alpha are supported when a shared thermoelastic property object is supplied; this benchmark uses a bounded internal component path rather than an external component validation.
This is a regression and integration benchmark, not external component validation.
